jobs.job: Answer a question about a stored claim with its evidence strata (asserted vs. what survived vs. what settled).

incumbent.statement: The LangGraph persistence docs describe only an undifferentiated 'Graph state snapshots' persisted per checkpoint ('checkpoints accumulate' during a long conversation); no strata distinction between asserted, surviving, and settled state is documented on the page.

house.statement: "Answers one cell question over an eavt row array with the entity's asserted and saturated counts, its settled section, its proof tree, and the closure/regime of the answer's fold."
house.artifact: @red-cup-engineering/ask-eavt-cell-service 0.3.0 README (also ask-eavt-trace-cell-service 0.3.0); served as metroplat 0.4.16's ask-eavt-cell / ask-eavt-trace-cell verbs on https://ops.561.group

jobs.reason: LangGraph's own docs expose one undifferentiated state snapshot per checkpoint; the house verb is deployed in production and returns asserted, saturated, and settled counts as three distinguishable strata for the same cell.

jobs.job: Return the proof path (provenance chain) of an answer as a first-class, content-addressed object.

incumbent.statement: "If you are familiar with OpenTelemetry, you can think of a run as a span." Runs/traces are described as hierarchical span-like data structures; no content-addressed identity (hash-based) for a run or trace is documented on the page.

house.statement: eavt 0.8.0's proof-tree citation resolution: "a claim as a Merkle DAG of ni:/entity-address/metroplat-artifact references, resolved as a flat {root, nodes} map ... never inlined"; ask-eavt-cell-service 0.3.0's example answer carries a proofTree object ({root, nodes, edges, missing, cycles, depth}).
house.artifact: @red-cup-engineering/eavt 0.8.0 package.json description (citationsOf/resolveProofTree/verifyProofClosure) and @red-cup-engineering/ask-eavt-cell-service 0.3.0 README worked example; served in the same ask-eavt-cell / ask-eavt-trace-cell verbs on https://ops.561.group

jobs.reason: LangSmith documents runs as OpenTelemetry-comparable spans with no content-addressed identity; the house proof tree resolves a claim as a Merkle DAG of RFC 6920 ni: references, served in the same production verb that answers the cell question.

jobs.job: Count and query held contradictions in the store.

incumbent.source: pages checked 2026-09-04; none documents a contradiction-counting or contradiction-query capability over stored facts

house.statement: "Reads one eavt trace file and counts the cells it settles as contradicted, or reports the trace absent." Production result cited in the 2026-09-01 founding note: "Over the two production traces the count is zero (8,312 theorem entities in 4 s; 10,453 carrier entities in 6 s)".
house.artifact: @red-cup-engineering/count-eavt-trace-contested-cells-service 0.1.1 README (also count-eavt-contested-cells-service 0.2.0 over a bare row array); served as metroplat 0.4.16's count-eavt-trace-contested-cells verb on https://ops.561.group

jobs.reason: no checked first-party LangChain/LangGraph/LangSmith surface documents contradiction counting or querying at all; the house verb is deployed and returns a real production count over two live traces (zero, pending a converse-predicate ledger to turn contradiction detection on).

jobs.job: Say that two predicates or relations are the same, at a graded strength with a price (SKOS closeMatch/exactMatch or the framework's equivalent).

incumbent.statement: LangChain's own retriever reference documents a continuous, unpriced similarity control rather than two named graded relations: "Threshold for determining when two documents are similar enough to be considered redundant. Defaults to `None`, must be specified if `k` is set to None." No first-party statement of a priced or two-tier (SKOS-equivalent) identification was found.

house.statement: "Prices the cheapest chain of mld or equal declarations identifying one predicate with another." GEODE's vocabulary generator: "an 'mld' chain prices as skos:closeMatch, an all-'equal' chain as skos:exactMatch", live at l-space.561.group/ns/predicate/part-of (skos:closeMatch and skos:exactMatch, 'the standard's own two strengths of match').
house.artifact: @red-cup-engineering/price-predicate-identification-service 0.1.0 README; served by @red-cup-engineering/geode 0.1.6's vocabulary.mjs on https://l-space.561.group/ns/predicate/part-of, but price-predicate-identification-service itself is not wired as a metroplat/ops.561.group verb (2026-09-01 founding note: ks-04 'not yet metroplat verbs' though 'also live on l-space')

jobs.reason: the pricing and SKOS serving are live on l-space.561.group, but the pricing service has no metroplat/ops.561.group verb of its own, so it is not on the same production surface as the other served jobs; LangChain has no first-party graded/priced identification concept to compare it against at all.

jobs.job: Tag an answer with the kind of settling that produced it (finite fold vs. limits vs. beyond).

incumbent.statement: no first-party statement found at https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/persistence: the page documents checkpoint storage backends (MemorySaver/SqliteSaver/PostgresSaver) and thread scoping but no tag naming the kind of process or closure that produced a given state.

house.statement: "eavt 0.8.0's stratify returns closure ({saturation, transfer, kappa, regime}) ... ask-eavt-cell 0.3.0 and ask-eavt-trace-cell 0.3.0 carry it, every current answer reading kappa 1, strict." Worked example: `"closure": {"saturation": 1, "transfer": 1, "kappa": 1, "regime": "strict"}, "regime": "strict"`.
house.artifact: @red-cup-engineering/eavt 0.8.0 (stratify) consumed by @red-cup-engineering/ask-eavt-cell-service 0.3.0 / ask-eavt-trace-cell-service 0.3.0 README; served in the same production ask-eavt-cell / ask-eavt-trace-cell verbs on https://ops.561.group

jobs.reason: LangGraph's own persistence docs tag a checkpoint with neither a process kind nor a closure classification; the house verb tags every answer with a closure ordinal and regime (strict, versus the honest classifier's unused aperiodic case), live in production.

incumbent.source: pages checked 2026-09-04; forum.langchain.com is community content, not a first-party surface, so it is recorded as a discovery lead only

jobs.job: Budget attention over what remains unreconciled (a read-next).

jobs.job: Read latency for one question over ~100k facts on a production host.

incumbent.statement: not published: https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/observability-concepts documents that runs carry timing ('threading keeps timing intact') but states no benchmark figure; LangGraph itself does not publish a single official latency benchmark. (Third-party benchmarks exist, e.g. a framework-overhead figure of roughly 10-14 ms per query reported by a 2026 aimultiple.com comparison, but that is a discovery lead, not first-party evidence, and the same source states most end-to-end latency is spent on model/tool I/O outside the framework, so it is not a comparable published number for this job.)
incumbent.source: https://docs.langchain.com/langsmith/observability-concepts (fetched 2026-09-04); third-party aimultiple.com benchmark noted but not used as incumbent evidence
